title: CLO 2024 Course: A Cozy Winter Cabin, Learn Home Goods Making with CLO!
description:
The temperature has dropped; unlock the warmth and comfort of winter with CLO~
CLO technology experts will guide you from making bedding sets, to techniques for rolling blankets and folding towels, helping you create a cozy and comfortable small room starting from the details!
Free materials are available on the CLO official WeChat account "CLO3D." Reply with "home" in the message to receive them.
transcript:
Homemade  
The theme of our live broadcast today is homemade products.  
It includes four sets of bedding, consisting of a duvet cover, a fitted sheet, pillows, pillowcases, a folding towel, a hanging towel, and a hair roll blanket.  
The rest are made of window curtains.  
Let's start making the four sets.  
First, we find the folder in the materials, then import the project file.  
The materials will also be shared later.  
After importing, there is already a board inside.  
If you don't have a board, you can create one using a lifting tool according to your size.  
Now I have imported the board.  
Let's start with the first one, the duvet cover.  
For other unused boards, we can select them with the middle and right mouse buttons to reverse activate them.  
This way, they will not participate in the simulation.  
Then we select the middle board and use the quick arrangement button to arrange it.  
Next, we move it to the area near the bed.  
Then adjust the positioning ball.  
The positioning ball I use shows the world coordinate.  
The positioning ball can be hidden in the 3D window by right-clicking to change its coordinate system.  
Then I use the hook and loop tool to hook the baseline on the duvet cover.  
Use the back key to hook the internal line.  
Then use the direct arrangement tool to fold it downward.  
Because we want to wrap this around the bed mattress.  
Then adjust the position.  
Now the bed mattress is activated.  
We want to reverse activate it; otherwise, it will conflict with the bed and cause unstable simulation.  
First, reverse activate this bed.  
The bed mattress is not reverse activated.  
Then we can switch to GPU simulation.  
We can use GPU simulation in version 2024.2.  
You can download the new version and try it.  
Then we switch.

So we use GPU simulation.  
Then start the simulation.

Simulate first.  
The simulation is good.

If the simulation effect is not good, we can test and adjust.  
Then simulate again.

Clone the board.

chunks.content: # CLO 2024 Course: A Cozy Winter Cabin - Home Goods Making with CLO This document details the step-by-step process of creating various home goods—including bedding sets, towels, quilts, pillows, blankets, bags, and window curtains—using CLO 3D software (version 2024.2). It covers importing project files, fabric simulation, adjusting pressure and friction settings, sewing, folding techniques, and material application, optimized for realistic simulation and visual effects. --- ## Bedding Set Creation: Duvet Cover and Quilt Simulation This section explains the setup and simulation of bedding components such as duvet covers and quilts, focusing on board arrangement, pressure adjustment, sewing, and GPU simulation for performance. - Import the project folder containing four bedding sets, including duvet cover, fitted sheet, pillows, pillowcases, towels, and a hair roll blanket. - After importing, if no board exists, create one using the lifting tool sized appropriately. - For the duvet cover: - Reverse activate unused boards with middle and right mouse buttons to exclude them from simulation. - Use the quick arrangement button to position the duvet cover near the bed. - Adjust the positioning ball (shows world coordinates; toggle visibility by right-clicking). - Use the hook and loop tool to attach the baseline of the duvet cover; hook the internal line with the back key. - Fold the duvet downward with the direct arrangement tool to wrap it around the bed mattress. - Reverse activate the bed mattress to prevent simulation conflicts. - Switch to GPU simulation (available in CLO 2024.2) for better performance with large fabrics. - Run simulation, divide the duvet into four sides, select these with the adjustment board tool, and add springs to improve wrapping. - Adjust spring boards vertically and set spring values (e.g., 8) to optimize fabric behavior. - Freeze the bed mattress once the simulation is satisfactory. - For the quilt: - Activate and arrange it near the bed mattress using the positioning ball. - Position the quilt slightly forward and below the front edge of the mattress. - Delete any bed film artifacts caused by previous activations. - Clone the quilt board to create inflation effects by adjusting pressure values: - Top board pressure reduced for softer puffiness. - Bottom board pressure set negative (e.g., -5) to prevent floating. - Test fabric types (e.g., cotton for relatively hard fabric) to improve simulation realism. - Use the W key and add fixed points to adjust the quilt’s shape. - Freeze the quilt once the desired posture is achieved. --- ## Quilt Folding Plates and Pillow Setup This section covers creating quilt folds and pillow details including sewing, pressure modification, and detailed edge effects for realism. - For quilt folding plates: - Select and arrange the folding plate on top of the quilt. - Untie and activate the plate, then sew the sewing line. - Simulate and adjust the folding plate position; pull locators to resolve overlaps. - Adjust pressure on top and bottom panels (e.g., top: -7, bottom: 2) to create swelling.

chunks.content: --- ## Quilt Folding Plates and Pillow Setup This section covers creating quilt folds and pillow details including sewing, pressure modification, and detailed edge effects for realism. - For quilt folding plates: - Select and arrange the folding plate on top of the quilt. - Untie and activate the plate, then sew the sewing line. - Simulate and adjust the folding plate position; pull locators to resolve overlaps. - Adjust pressure on top and bottom panels (e.g., top: -7, bottom: 2) to create swelling. - Reduce particle diameter on the panel for smoother appearance. - After simulation, freeze and group the boards. - Pillow creation: - Quickly arrange pillow boards near the bed and activate. - Adjust pressure values positively or negatively to control swelling (e.g., bottom: -10, top: 10). - Reduce particle diameter for delicate movement and better visual effect. - Create flower edge effects by clearing joints and expanding the board edge. - Cut excess powder lines and use free powder to create seams between pillow plates. - Harden edges for stability, then simulate. - Adjust pillow positioning with the positioning ball and freeze once finalized. - Duplicate and reposition pillows for overall bed arrangement. --- ## Towel Folding and Hanging Techniques This section explains towel folding methods using CLO’s folding tools and simulation settings to achieve realistic towel stacks and hanging effects. - Prepare towel boards by moving and hiding shelves for workspace clarity. - Use the folding 3D clothing tool: - Rotate on X-axis or horizontally flip towels. - Draw fold lines by double-clicking the board and folding red regions. - Use Shift to draw horizontal fold lines. - Adjust fabric friction coefficient to reduce sliding and deformation (increase friction for better grip). - Perform multiple folds, simulating after each to check fabric behavior. - Use the little brick tool to adjust towel position for stacked towel effects. - Copy the towel board to create layered stacks and simulate weight effects pressing down. - For hanging towels: - Reset 3D arrangement to flat. - Use fold-and-pick options to fold sides separately. - Draw fold-and-pick lines to simulate hanging and natural fabric fall on towel racks. - Adjust positioning locators to avoid overlap and improve hanging effect. - Pull simulation meshes gently to resolve conflicts with virtual shelf models. --- ## Blanket Rolling and Sectional Simulation This section presents techniques to simulate rolling blankets in sections, optimizing fabric thickness, friction, and sewing for realistic roll-up effects. - Import blanket materials and project files. - Because long blankets can be inconvenient to roll, divide the blanket into three or four sections using inner lines and cutting tools. - Turn off visibility on later sections and focus on front part: - Double-click to add pins and simulate rolling. - Cancel hardening to keep fabric soft during rolling. - Adjust fabric thickness (e.g., increase to 5) and friction coefficient to improve roll stability and prevent sliding. - Remove pins after simulation and freeze the rolled section.

set flange type to fold. - Delete all fixing pins before simulation. - After simulating to raise the bag model, untie the hairpin but do not simulate untie action. - Move original model down into hairpin, zoom in, and simulate shrinking effect. - Use editor monitor to check details like "gold sand," adjusting to decrease and bring closer gradually. - Rotate model slightly and switch to texture surface view. - Sew stickers on panels using edge sewing tool; freeze other boards during sewing. - Apply texture surfaces and add mold lines on both sides with the line tool. - Modify line properties such as shoulder distance, thickness, and color via attribute editor. - Set 3D and grid surfaces to ‘all’ for clear texture effects. - The mold for the bag is completed. --- ## Window Curtain Assembly and Windbreaker Effect This section covers importing window curtain projects, dividing large panels, creating windbreaker folding effects, sewing, applying materials, and adding detailed components like buttons and curtain poles. - Import the window curtain project file. - Window curtains consist of two panels: a small top panel and a larger bottom panel. - Divide large panels into parts for easier handling, simulating folding windbreaker effects with the folding arrangement tool. - Cut round panels and freeze them as fixed groups. - Copy and paste groups to create multiple curtain sections, adjusting placements accordingly. - Merge sewing lines to unify panels into whole boards. - Delete unnecessary inner lines and freeze completed sections. - Adjust particle diameter for delicate simulation (e.g., 5-8 mm).

markdown_content: # CLO 2024 Course: A Cozy Winter Cabin - Home Goods Making with CLO This document details the step-by-step process of creating various home goods—including bedding sets, towels, quilts, pillows, blankets, bags, and window curtains—using CLO 3D software (version 2024.2). It covers importing project files, fabric simulation, adjusting pressure and friction settings, sewing, folding techniques, and material application, optimized for realistic simulation and visual effects. --- ## Bedding Set Creation: Duvet Cover and Quilt Simulation This section explains the setup and simulation of bedding components such as duvet covers and quilts, focusing on board arrangement, pressure adjustment, sewing, and GPU simulation for performance. - Import the project folder containing four bedding sets, including duvet cover, fitted sheet, pillows, pillowcases, towels, and a hair roll blanket. - After importing, if no board exists, create one using the lifting tool sized appropriately. - For the duvet cover: - Reverse activate unused boards with middle and right mouse buttons to exclude them from simulation. - Use the quick arrangement button to position the duvet cover near the bed. - Adjust the positioning ball (shows world coordinates; toggle visibility by right-clicking). - Use the hook and loop tool to attach the baseline of the duvet cover; hook the internal line with the back key. - Fold the duvet downward with the direct arrangement tool to wrap it around the bed mattress. - Reverse activate the bed mattress to prevent simulation conflicts. - Switch to GPU simulation (available in CLO 2024.2) for better performance with large fabrics. - Run simulation, divide the duvet into four sides, select these with the adjustment board tool, and add springs to improve wrapping. - Adjust spring boards vertically and set spring values (e.g., 8) to optimize fabric behavior. - Freeze the bed mattress once the simulation is satisfactory. - For the quilt: - Activate and arrange it near the bed mattress using the positioning ball. - Position the quilt slightly forward and below the front edge of the mattress. - Delete any bed film artifacts caused by previous activations. - Clone the quilt board to create inflation effects by adjusting pressure values: - Top board pressure reduced for softer puffiness. - Bottom board pressure set negative (e.g., -5) to prevent floating. - Test fabric types (e.g., cotton for relatively hard fabric) to improve simulation realism. - Use the W key and add fixed points to adjust the quilt’s shape. - Freeze the quilt once the desired posture is achieved. --- ## Quilt Folding Plates and Pillow Setup This section covers creating quilt folds and pillow details including sewing, pressure modification, and detailed edge effects for realism. - For quilt folding plates: - Select and arrange the folding plate on top of the quilt. - Untie and activate the plate, then sew the sewing line. - Simulate and adjust the folding plate position; pull locators to resolve overlaps. - Adjust pressure on top and bottom panels (e.g., top: -7, bottom: 2) to create swelling. - Reduce particle diameter on the panel for smoother appearance. - After simulation, freeze and group the boards. - Pillow creation: - Quickly arrange pillow boards near the bed and activate. - Adjust pressure values positively or negatively to control swelling (e.g., bottom: -10, top: 10). - Reduce particle diameter for delicate movement and better visual effect. - Create flower edge effects by clearing joints and expanding the board edge. - Cut excess powder lines and use free powder to create seams between pillow plates. - Harden edges for stability, then simulate. - Adjust pillow positioning with the positioning ball and freeze once finalized. - Duplicate and reposition pillows for overall bed arrangement. --- ## Towel Folding and Hanging Techniques This section explains towel folding methods using CLO’s folding tools and simulation settings to achieve realistic towel stacks and hanging effects. - Prepare towel boards by moving and hiding shelves for workspace clarity. - Use the folding 3D clothing tool: - Rotate on X-axis or horizontally flip towels. - Draw fold lines by double-clicking the board and folding red regions. - Use Shift to draw horizontal fold lines. - Adjust fabric friction coefficient to reduce sliding and deformation (increase friction for better grip). - Perform multiple folds, simulating after each to check fabric behavior. - Use the little brick tool to adjust towel position for stacked towel effects. - Copy the towel board to create layered stacks and simulate weight effects pressing down. - For hanging towels: - Reset 3D arrangement to flat. - Use fold-and-pick options to fold sides separately. - Draw fold-and-pick lines to simulate hanging and natural fabric fall on towel racks. - Adjust positioning locators to avoid overlap and improve hanging effect. - Pull simulation meshes gently to resolve conflicts with virtual shelf models. --- ## Blanket Rolling and Sectional Simulation This section presents techniques to simulate rolling blankets in sections, optimizing fabric thickness, friction, and sewing for realistic roll-up effects. - Import blanket materials and project files. - Because long blankets can be inconvenient to roll, divide the blanket into three or four sections using inner lines and cutting tools. - Turn off visibility on later sections and focus on front part: - Double-click to add pins and simulate rolling. - Cancel hardening to keep fabric soft during rolling. - Adjust fabric thickness (e.g., increase to 5) and friction coefficient to improve roll stability and prevent sliding. - Remove pins after simulation and freeze the rolled section. - Repeat process for second and third sections: - Sew ends and simulate rolling. - Slightly increase pressure for faster rolling. - Freeze each section after simulation. - Merge panels using the edit sewing line tool to unify the blanket. - Adjust uneven ends by simulating and pulling fabric to flatten. - Freeze the final rolled blanket. --- ## Bag Model Creation and Simulation This section details construction and simulation of a hair roll bag, including internal lines, folding, fixed points, flange application, and shrinking effects. - Position hairpin board at ground center using right-click move. - Move bag panel under hairpin and activate. - Create internal lines matching bag shape on both sides. - Use folding arrangement tool to fold and arrange the bag for better simulation. - Hold W key and add fixed points on both sides before simulation to bring sides closer. - Delete unnecessary internal lines. - Use flange tool to fix upper and lower bag sections; set flange type to fold. - Delete all fixing pins before simulation. - After simulating to raise the bag model, untie the hairpin but do not simulate untie action. - Move original model down into hairpin, zoom in, and simulate shrinking effect. - Use editor monitor to check details like "gold sand," adjusting to decrease and bring closer gradually. - Rotate model slightly and switch to texture surface view. - Sew stickers on panels using edge sewing tool; freeze other boards during sewing. - Apply texture surfaces and add mold lines on both sides with the line tool. - Modify line properties such as shoulder distance, thickness, and color via attribute editor. - Set 3D and grid surfaces to ‘all’ for clear texture effects. - The mold for the bag is completed. --- ## Window Curtain Assembly and Windbreaker Effect This section covers importing window curtain projects, dividing large panels, creating windbreaker folding effects, sewing, applying materials, and adding detailed components like buttons and curtain poles. - Import the window curtain project file. - Window curtains consist of two panels: a small top panel and a larger bottom panel. - Divide large panels into parts for easier handling, simulating folding windbreaker effects with the folding arrangement tool. - Cut round panels and freeze them as fixed groups. - Copy and paste groups to create multiple curtain sections, adjusting placements accordingly. - Merge sewing lines to unify panels into whole boards. - Delete unnecessary inner lines and freeze completed sections. - Adjust particle diameter for delicate simulation (e.g., 5-8 mm). - Apply cotton fabric for softness and better drape. - For double-layer effects, carve out inside layers and simulate separately, hardening and freezing as needed. - Hook basic lines into internal lines using right-click ‘hook as fan’ to group edges. - Sew bottom and side seams using thread break powder. - Change flange types to fold on sewn edges. - Manually sew flanges on panels that are not face-moving boards. - Place curtain boards far apart after sewing, add to inside in 3D window, and freeze. - Simulate sides separately to adjust swelling effects by reducing particle diameter and collision. - Place curtain pole near air holes; air holes are modeled with button tools. - Add buttons, select air eye type, adjust size (e.g., 32), and sink buttons into the board by negative line type values. - Apply new fabric with transparency set to zero for hollow effect. - Add details like name lines using free name line tools. - Delete or keep inner lines as preferred. - Freeze and unlock all components. - Copy and mirror curtains to complete symmetrical pairs. - Use editing tools to adjust sizes and positions. - Add glass layers behind curtains to complete the window setup. --- # Summary This guide comprehensively documents the CLO 2024.2 workflow for designing and simulating detailed home goods including bedding, towels, blankets, bags, and curtains. It emphasizes practical use of CLO’s simulation tools such as GPU acceleration, pressure and friction adjustments, sewing techniques, folding operations, and fabric/material management to achieve realistic draping and structural effects.
